name: THREAT Matrix experimental scoring overlay
notice: Experimental and non-normative. These values are authored, type-level estimates for classes of behavior. They have not been validated against outcomes or by independent human reviewers. They do not predict violence, they are not a score of any person, and they must not be used as grounds for adverse action. The vocabulary in framework.json is complete without this file.

rubric.composite_math: Recommended composite is the geometric mean of the four type-level potentials, with detectability flipped to reflect its mitigating role: type_weight = (impact_potential × blast_radius_potential × recoverability_inverse × (10 - detectability))^(1/4). The geometric mean ensures the composite is bounded 0.0-10.0 and that a weak value on any single axis pulls the composite down, appropriate for security-intuitive 'weakest-link' reading. Detectability is flipped because high observability by trained personnel reduces (not raises) the realized escalation potential. Consumers may substitute weighted-additive or other variants with documented rationale per CONTRIBUTING.md 'Schema design principles.'

type_band_floor_rule.definition: A triage floor layered on the severity math: an indicator whose behavior applies DIRECT PHYSICAL FORCE to a person's body carries type_band = critical at minimum, regardless of its computed type_weight. type_weight is unchanged, it remains the true severity computation, so the gradient between a single assault (~4.6) and a mass bombing (~8.7) is preserved, but the triage band for any force against a person is critical. Such indicators carry a `type_band_floor` field set to "critical". Rationale: a casualty is critical regardless of scale. The severity math gates the top band on blast_radius (population scope), which would place a single-victim killing at high and reserve critical for mass-casualty events; but for triage, any application of force to a person is a top-priority event. Count is a severity GRADIENT (in type_weight), not the critical THRESHOLD. This is a values/triage rule, not a change to the weight formula.
type_band_floor_rule.applies_to: Behaviors that directly apply physical force to a person: weapon discharge, vehicle ramming, explosive detonation, physical assault, overpowering or incapacitating personnel, taking physical custody by restraint, forcible extraction, and physical restraint or force against a captive. Also included (extension of 2026-07-28): taking or maintaining custody or control of a person by weapon threat or credible threat of immediate force during in-progress execution, where a weapon is displayed at the victim and control is being established or maintained. SCOPE GUARD: threatened force WITHOUT the custody or control context does not floor: a weapon brandished during a dispute, or a communicated or conditional threat made outside an in-progress seizure, is carried by the type-level type_weight and instance conditioning, not by the floor. This narrow extension follows the precedent discipline of the V1.4 infrastructure type_band_floor extension (narrow, mechanism-specific; 2026-07-18). DOCUMENTED POPULATION AND EXTENSIONS. The floor is carried by 43 indicators: 11 person, 24 facility, 8 infrastructure. Person, direct force: IND-0301-01, IND-0301-02, IND-0301-03, IND-0301-04, IND-0302-03, IND-0303-01, IND-0303-03, IND-0303-04, IND-0304-01, IND-0304-03, IND-0306-02. Facility, direct force: IND-F0203-04, IND-F0204-05, IND-F0302-02, IND-F0305-01, IND-F0305-03, IND-F0306-04, IND-F0309-05. Facility extension 1, secondary strike (an indicator that positions a second strike against responders or evacuees during an active incident): IND-F0309-03, IND-F0408-01, IND-F0408-02, IND-F0408-04. Facility extension 2, occupied-structure harm (execution behaviors that harm occupants through the structure or its systems, such as incendiary attack, structural sabotage, contamination of air or water, and blocked exits): IND-F0301-01, IND-F0301-02, IND-F0301-05, IND-F0303-01, IND-F0303-02, IND-F0303-04, IND-F0304-02, IND-F0304-05, IND-F0308-01, IND-F0308-02, IND-F0308-04, IND-F0308-05, IND-F0309-01. Infrastructure extension, life-safety mechanisms (execution behaviors that defeat a safety system or manipulate a treatment or control process so that casualties are the direct mechanism): IND-I0302-01, IND-I0302-02, IND-I0302-04, IND-I0302-05, IND-I0304-05, IND-I0306-01, IND-I0306-03, IND-I0306-05. KNOWN INCONSISTENCIES, UNRESOLVED: IND-F0302-05 (second device on evacuation or responder routes) is not floored while IND-F0309-03 is; IND-I0306-02 (raw water intake contamination) is not floored while IND-I0306-01, IND-I0306-03, and IND-I0306-05 are; IND-0304-04 is not floored while IND-0304-01 and IND-0304-03 are. They are listed so a consumer can reproduce the published set exactly.

detectability_guidance.flip_rationale: Detectability enters the composite INVERTED ((10 - detectability)) by design: high observability by trained personnel shrinks expected residual harm because an interdiction window exists, while stealth removes that window. This matches the CVSS and insider-threat convention of conditioning realized risk on observability. The composite therefore reads as EXPECTED RESIDUAL HARM, not raw severity: a stealthy indicator class outweighs an equally harmful conspicuous one because it is less likely to be interrupted.
detectability_guidance.misread_guard: Do not read a high weight on a stealthy class as 'stealth is severe.' Stealth is not severity: it is the removal of the interdiction discount. The severity content lives in impact_potential, blast_radius_potential, and recoverability_inverse; detectability only conditions how much of it is expected to survive countermeasures.
detectability_guidance.self_censoring_caveat: Detectability is a self-censoring axis: the stealthiest behavior classes are systematically the least observed and least reported, so their authored detectability values rest on the thinnest observational base. Treat very-low detectability values as carrying wider uncertainty than the rest of the rubric.
detectability_guidance.added: V1.3 (2026-07-09), documenting the standing formula; no formula change.
detectability_guidance.aftermath_note: In aftermath, the interdiction window is over the actor, not the harm: detectability conditions attribution and re-attack prevention rather than harm interdiction; the flip's direction is unchanged.

blast_radius_guidance.definition: blast_radius_potential encodes TOTAL expected victim scope for the indicator class: intended targets PLUS expected collateral (bystander / non-target) casualties. It is not intended-victim count alone, a single-target attack can carry high blast_radius when its method produces collateral (a bombing that kills one intended target and nearby bystanders scores high, not low). Method sets the type-level base rate below; venue, timing, and crowd density modulate at assessment (instance) time.

method_collateral_base_rates.note: Recommended type-level anchors (0.0-10.0) for the attack method a class embodies or presages. Combine with intended-target scope, a mass-casualty-intended attack raises blast_radius above the collateral base rate, and deviate for sub-type. These are the People matrix values. The Facility calibration shares them; Organization and Infrastructure re-derive their own.

blast_radius_guidance.authoring_notes: Pre-attack indicators inherit the collateral ceiling of the method they presage (acquiring an explosive takes the explosive base rate). Venue-selection and timing signals are bystander-risk indicators even in target-development and mobilization phases, an approach timed to a crowd event, or a firing position with line-of-sight to a gathering. The People matrix models bystanders as a distinct population in tactic TM0306 (Bystander Management); this axis carries the SEVERITY of that exposure, which TM0306 alone does not. Instance-level venue and crowd-density conditioning belongs in the assessment layer, not the type-level base rate.

collateral_reveal_guidance.principle: Collateral-revealed, the parallel to method-revealed: raise blast_radius above the single-victim / method-base floor only where the BEHAVIOR ITSELF observably reveals a group/population target or a public/crowd venue. Do NOT uplift on mere compatibility with a group target (e.g., a target_identity that merely permits a group), that over-applies and collapses toward a blanket floor. A behavior against a single individual in an unrevealed venue keeps the floor.

tiers.indiscriminate_or_population_target_reve: mass ceiling 7.0-9.0, combined with the method base rate
tiers.public_or_crowd_venue_revealed: 5.0-7.0: line-of-sight to a gathering, approach timed to a crowd event, an attack staged in a crowded venue
tiers.bystanders_present_or_managed: 4.0-5.0: bystander-management behaviors, or occupation/siege of a public site
tiers.cohesive_group_or_affinity_target_reveal: 3.5-4.0: a specific cohesive group, not a crowd
tiers.single_individual_or_venue_unrevealed: method base rate or single-victim floor (2.5-3.0; covert or targeted-poison methods sit at the 2.0 base rate)

collateral_reveal_guidance.instance_deferral: The statistical likelihood that an unrevealed-venue targeted attack produces bystander casualties is an INSTANCE-level assessment: it depends on the specific target's typical environment (a public figure in crowds vs. a private individual), and is resolved at assessment time in the instance-conditioning layer, NOT encoded in the type-level blast_radius. Keeping the type-level floor for unrevealed venues is deliberate, not an omission.
collateral_reveal_guidance.computed_critical_requires_both: blast_radius (collateral) alone does not produce a critical band VIA THE COMPUTED WEIGHT: the geometric mean still requires strong showings on multiple axes. Under the original equal-quartile critical cut (7.5), computed-critical required BOTH mass-lethal impact_potential AND mass blast_radius; the rubric v1.2.0 recalibration (critical=6.5) relaxes this at the margin: a behavior combining mass blast_radius with substantial but not mass-lethal impact_potential (e.g., in-execution positioning or bystander-exposure behaviors weighing 6.5-7.5) now computes critical. NOTE: this concerns the computed weight only; the separate type_band_floor_rule floors any direct-physical-force-on-a-person behavior to critical regardless of computed weight (a casualty is critical at any scale).

blast_radius_guidance.authoring_status: Added rubric v1.1.0 (2026-07-04). V1.3: the collateral re-authoring landed matrix-wide. The execution phase is scored (mass methods 8.0-9.0) and pre-attack indicators inherit their method-collateral ceiling; the phase-1/2 breach/penetration/access-elevation set was moved off the single-victim floor to the occupied-environment collateral tier (perimeter 5.0, zone-penetration 5.5, access-elevation 5.0) - a defeated control exposes the population behind it. Remaining 2.5-3.0 values are genuinely single-victim / low-collateral by design (kidnapping, captive control, in-execution support, and the detection-artifact audit anomalies IND-0205-04/06), not un-re-authored. Blast re-authoring: complete.

aftermath_rule.rule: An aftermath (Phase-4) behavior's blast_radius_potential encodes ONLY the victim or stakeholder scope it presages or enables GOING FORWARD (a next attack, continued harm, or renewed operation). The scope of the completed attack belongs to the execution-phase indicators, not to the aftermath behaviors that follow it. An aftermath behavior that merely echoes or references the just-completed attack does not inherit that attack's scope; it is scored on what it itself produces or enables forward. The same forward-looking test governs aftermath impact_potential.
aftermath_rule.facility_floor_scope: The Facility blast floor (base rate ~4.0, facilities admit mass-casualty by default) is a property of behaviors aimed at or presaging harm to the venue. It governs Phases 1-3 and forward-looking Phase-4 behaviors (secondary device, re-attack positioning, coercive demand). It does NOT bind aftermath pure trace (withdrawal, evidence management, cover, network protection, financial disposition, after-action, counter-forensics), which take the cross-matrix trace floor (~2.5; IND-F0402-04 sits at 4.0 and is an unresolved exception). Promoted here from the V1.3 CHANGELOG calibration prose into the rubric proper.
aftermath_rule.copycat_tier: Narrow: only explicitly instructional or celebratory copycat-enablement content (a how-to breakdown of the tactics used, or content celebrating and elevating copycat attempts) inherits a discounted forward scope (one tier above the trace floor, not full execution scope). Generic amplification and plain attribution do NOT qualify; they take the trace floor.
aftermath_rule.claims_rule: A claim of responsibility that includes a threat of continuation gets NO blast uplift on the attribution class. The attribution behavior takes the trace floor; the continuation content is carried by the coercive-demand class and connected through correlates_with, not by inflating the attribution score.
aftermath_rule.audience_vs_victims_guard: Reach counts only insofar as the reached population is the harmed population. An aftermath communication's readership is not by itself victim or stakeholder harm; a behavior carries the scope of the harm it produces, not the size of the audience that observes it. This is the line that separates continuing-harm aftermath behaviors from trace aftermath behaviors.
aftermath_rule.anti_harmonization_guard: After this reconciliation, same-named messaging and amplification classes are deliberately scored differently across matrices: the Organizations continuing-harm classes (audience amplification, narrative laundering, coercive follow-through, recruitment and momentum) keep elevated blast because in the institutional harm model the harm production is ongoing (see calibration_guidance, aftermath seam reconciliation), while the same-named Person, Facility, and Infrastructure classes take the trace floor (the narrow copycat tier). This asymmetry is the harm-model difference working as designed. Do NOT harmonize these classes in any future authoring pass.

axis_confidence_rubric.levels: established: the value sits on a documented evidentiary anchor. inferred: the value is a reasoned assignment without a documented anchor, the honest default. thin: the value carries wider uncertainty and is a candidate for earlier human review.
axis_confidence_rubric.derivation_rules: Rule-derived by scripts/analysis/derive-axis-confidence.py, never hand-tuned. detectability: value at or below 2.0 derives thin (the self_censoring_caveat band, where very low detectability values carry wider uncertainty); at or above 6.0 derives established; otherwise inferred. blast_radius_potential: value within 0.5 of a documented base-rate anchor or tier bound for that matrix (People method_collateral_base_rates, which the Facility calibration shares; Organization tier bounds 2.0, 3.5, 4.0, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5; Infrastructure tier bounds 2.5, 3.5, 4.0, 5.5, 6.0, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, 9.0; People and Facility anchors 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0, 7.0, 8.0, 9.0) derives established; otherwise inferred. impact_potential and recoverability_inverse: inferred framework-wide, the honest default; upgrading them is future evidence-audit work.
axis_confidence_rubric.misread_guard: Confidence is evidence basis, NOT severity. A thin axis is a wider error bar and a candidate for earlier human review. It is NEVER an automatic demotion: discounting a score because an axis is thin is a computed capability discount by the back door, banned per instance_conditioning.

rubric.calibration_guidance: Current thresholds on the stored two-decimal type_weight: medium 3.0, high 5.0, critical 6.5. The band is derived from the stored rounded weight, then raised to the floor where one is set. The current population is 14 low, 435 medium, 291 high, 88 critical. History follows. The type_band_thresholds above reflect the rubric v1.2.0 recalibration against the realized scored population (V1.3, 390 indicators): at that recalibration medium and high kept the original equal-quartile cuts (2.5 / 5.0); the critical threshold was lowered from the equal-quartile 7.5 to 6.5 so the critical band carries a weight-driven population: under the 7.5 cut, two-thirds of critical-band indicators reached the band only via the type_band_floor rule. Consumers SHOULD calibrate the thresholds to their threat-posture environment for best results. Higher-posture environments (e.g., critical infrastructure, executive protection, dignitary protection) may shift `high` and `critical` thresholds downward (e.g., high=4.0, critical=6.0) to surface medium-weight indicators earlier in triage. Lower-posture environments may shift them upward. Document the rationale for any deviation per CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles". Aftermath seam reconciliation (2026-07-28): aftermath blast and impact encode only forward-looking (presaged or enabled) scope, not the completed attack's scope, and the Facility mass-casualty blast floor governs Phases 1-3 and forward-looking Phase 4 only, not aftermath trace. 165 indicators were re-authored to the trace floor (66 moving high to medium); the Organizations continuing-harm classes and the narrow copycat-enablement tier stay elevated by design (see blast_radius_guidance.aftermath_rule). Bottom-cut recalibration (2026-07-28): the medium threshold was raised 2.5 to 3.0 against the realized post-reconciliation population. The low band had held zero of 815 indicators (the count at V1.6), an equal-quartile cut never recalibrated at the bottom (the v1.2.0 pass corrected only the top, critical 7.5 to 6.5); the bottom population's severity axes were already at honest floors, propped above 2.5 only by the stealth term (10 minus detectability). Adopted low-band definition: behaviors whose direct residual harm is investigative or attributional trace (egress, cleanup, attribution, ambient pre-operational recon) rather than realized or imminently enabled harm. 15 indicators move from medium to low; the high and critical thresholds are unchanged (5.0 and 6.5). A targeted weight review of the two lowest organization target-development signals followed: IND-O0101-02 (fixation escalation) was re-tiered on impact (3.0 to 4.5, the presages-a-targeted-campaign tier) and now bands medium, while IND-O0101-04 (pre-commitment identifier collection) is confirmed correctly low as ambient pre-operational recon.

instance_conditioning.layer: Layer 2 (instance) of the type/instance split: CVSS Base-vs-Environmental. Layer 1 (axes / type_weight / type_band and informs_axes) scores the indicator CLASS; Layer 2 conditions that type score for a specific case (this actor, this target, now). The framework DEFINES this layer (scoring-overlay.schema.json $defs instance_assessment and scored_case_record) and ships NO instances; consumers hold the per-case records.
instance_conditioning.escalate_only_rule: Instance conditioning may RAISE a case's priority above the type band: to catch the false-LOW, a mild-looking type with an alarming instance, which is the deadliest error: but may NEVER lower it below the type band. There is no computed capability discount: means_in_hand='unknown' is the safe default and does not demote a case. The floor is enforced in two layers, since schema alone cannot do all of it: the conditional subschemas on scored_case_record reject a conditioned_priority below the stated type_band, and the reference validator plus the consumer SDK enforce band fidelity, that type_band equals the authored type_band of the indicator at a stated framework version. The held-vs-raised distinction is derived by comparison (raised iff conditioned_priority exceeds type_band), never stored as a separate flag.
instance_conditioning.demotion_doctrine: The conditioned priority is an escalation detector, not a queue-ranking model; de-prioritization is a case-management decision that must never be written back into the score. This answers the volume objection: at scale, cases leave the queue by DISPOSITION (closure, monitoring tiers), never by score demotion. A demotion path would let capability discounts in through the back door. The disposition is recorded in the structured scored_case_record.disposition field (for example disrupted_by_interdiction, closed_benign, or a monitoring tier), alongside the score and never inside it. Note also that source_credibility measures reporting reliability, not hostile-attribution confidence: whether a hostile actor exists at all is a separate judgment carried by primary_objective_evidence_tier, whose 'contested' value marks a disputed attribution.

raise_guidance.purpose: Advisory patterns for inter-analyst consistency, NOT a formula. Nothing here is computed and the escalate-only invariant is unchanged: these patterns describe when analysts typically raise, and a raise is always a human call.
patterns: specific_target with means_in_hand assessed_present or confirmed_present: raise at least one band.
The preceding pattern with tempo_trajectory accelerating: consider critical.
proximity_access has_access or at_or_near_target with specific_target: strong raise signal.
pathway_stage at or beyond preparation with target_focus narrowing: consider a raise.
source_credibility low: hold pending corroboration; the band still floors at type.

instance_conditioning.inhibitors_exclusion: Protective factors and inhibitors (stabilizers, stake in conformity) are DELIBERATELY absent from the instance record. Under escalate-only they have no mechanical role: they only argue a case down, and they are the field's most misjudged, most gameable variable. Readers from SPJ traditions (WAVR-21, HCR-20) should read the record as deliberately asymmetric, not incomplete. Inhibitors inform case management, which sits outside the score.
instance_conditioning.binding_contract: A type score becomes a case assessment only when joined to its instance record: the scored_case_record object requires both. Wherever a score drives case operations (queue ranking, dashboards, handoffs, API triage) it must carry, or be joined to, its instance record. A bare type number rendered without one (including in the reference SPA, which displays Layer-1 taxonomy) is a Layer-1 datum, not an assessment of any case. A conditioned assessment is valid only when its type_band equals the authored type_band of indicator_id at a stated framework version: a consumer cannot launder a floor by misquoting the band, and the reference validator performs this cross reference.
instance_conditioning.conditioning_guidance: Indicators carry conditioning_guidance: framework-provided default investigative tasking naming the instance factors that are the hidden drivers of danger for that behavior (probe_factors, machine-filterable) with a practitioner directive (guidance). A starting point for consumer playbooks, intended for composition across combinations of observed indicators; consumers may follow, extend, or override it with their own procedures. Authored across all indicators (815 at V1.6, 828 at V1.7); replaces the retired informs-keyed instance_conditioning_hints pilot.
instance_conditioning.status: Contract defined V1.3 (2026-07-09); completed V1.6: sixth factor proximity_access added, demotion doctrine, raise guidance, inhibitors exclusion, and credibility articulation recorded (2026-07-28). The consumer/UI instance-entry surface remains deferred.
instance_conditioning.provenance: Scoring review of the structured instance record and the display-binding contract; contract completed 2026-07-28 (demotion doctrine, raise guidance, proximity_access, inhibitors exclusion, credibility articulation). See docs/METHODOLOGY.md.
